exposure: Implementation of Robson classification system (pre- vs post-intervention period)
outcome: Distribution of CS across Robson groups
Trends and relative contributions of Robson groups to CS burden
cohort: The study included 20,270 deliveries from a tertiary maternity unit in Ghana, with a mean maternal age of 28.6 years.
finding: The implementation of the Robson classification identified specific characteristics of women associated with increased caesarean births, namely nulliparous or multiparous women with spontaneous labour and no uterine scar (groups 1 and 3), and those with preterm gestation including a previous uterine scar (group 10), which all saw statistically significant increases in CS rates in the post-intervention phase.
mod_finding: Overall caesarean section rates constituted 40.1% of all deliveries, with rates highest in Robson group 9 and lowest in group 3, and statistically significant increases observed in CS rates for groups 1, 3, and 10 after the implementation of the Robson classification.
